topic: Why Thailand Is Stranger Than You Think
hook: Your car swaps sides of the road on a bridge between Thailand and Laos.
title: Why Thailand Is Stranger Than You Think
description:
Thailand lives in the year 2569, has a city named after Ayodhya, and has a bridge where cars swap sides of the road. Here are seven strange facts about Thailand that sound fake and are true, from a train running through a market to a monkey banquet. Watch to the end for the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge.

#Thailand #Geography #FactsThatSoundFake
tags: Thailand is stranger than you think
comment_prompt: Which Thailand fact surprised you most?

scenes.narration: Your car swaps sides of the road on a bridge between Thailand and Laos.
scenes.headline: Cars Swap Sides

scenes.narration: Thailand is full of facts like this, where the real thing sounds more fake than anything you could make up.
scenes.headline: True, Not Fake

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see seven strange true facts, from a year that reads 2569 to a train running through a market.
scenes.headline: Seven Strange Facts

scenes.narration: The bridge is saved for last, because it is the one that breaks your brain.
scenes.headline: Saved For Last

scenes.narration: Each fact is stranger than the one before, so do not leave after the first one.
scenes.headline: Stranger Each Time

scenes.narration: We start with the date on a Thai calendar today.
scenes.headline: Thai Calendar

scenes.narration: Fact one. Open a Thai calendar today and it does not say 2026. It says 2569.
scenes.headline: It Says 2569

scenes.narration: Thailand officially counts years from the Buddha's passing, which puts it 543 years ahead of the calendar on your phone.
scenes.headline: 543 Years Ahead

scenes.narration: Next January, the Thai year will tick over to 2570 while yours reads 2027.
scenes.headline: Year 2570 Next

scenes.narration: Their traditional new year, Songkran, comes in April, and the whole country turns into a giant water fight.
scenes.headline: Songkran Water Fight

scenes.narration: The name Songkran comes from Sanskrit, the same root as India's Sankranti.
scenes.headline: Same Sanskrit Root

scenes.narration: Strangers throw buckets of water at you on the road, and it is meant as a blessing, not an attack.
scenes.headline: Water As Blessing

scenes.narration: Thailand also has no daylight saving, so its clocks sit one and a half hours ahead of India all year.
scenes.headline: Ahead Of India

scenes.narration: Easy trick: Thai time is Indian time plus ninety minutes, so seven in the evening in Delhi is half past eight there.
scenes.headline: 7 PM Becomes 8:30

scenes.narration: Stranger still, Thailand has a city named after a place you know well, and its kings share a name with Lord Ram.
scenes.headline: A Familiar Name

scenes.narration: Stay with me, because that one is next.
scenes.headline: Up Next

scenes.narration: Fact two. A Thai city is named after Ayodhya, and its kings are called Rama.
scenes.headline: Ayutthaya = Ayodhya

scenes.narration: Ayutthaya was the old capital of the kingdom, and its name comes from Ayodhya, the city of Lord Ram.
scenes.headline: Old Capital

scenes.narration: Thailand's national epic, the Ramakien, is its own version of the Ramayana, with Hanuman, Ravana and Sita all in it.
scenes.headline: Thai Ramayana

scenes.narration: Walk into the Grand Palace temple in Bangkok and you will see giant demon guardians from this story standing at the gates.
scenes.headline: Demon Guardians

scenes.narration: The ruling Chakri dynasty gives every king the title Rama, and the current king is Rama the Tenth.
scenes.headline: King Rama X

scenes.narration: Thailand is a Buddhist country, yet its main airport is called Suvarnabhumi, Sanskrit for golden land.
scenes.headline: Golden Land Airport

scenes.narration: Thai dancers still perform the Ramakien on stage, in masks and gold costumes.
scenes.headline: Masked Dancers

scenes.narration: So an Indian visitor can land in Bangkok and feel oddly at home before leaving the airport.
scenes.headline: Oddly Familiar

scenes.narration: But Thailand also did something almost no neighbour managed, and it is the next fact.
scenes.headline: What Others Could Not

scenes.narration: It involves foreign ships, clever kings, and a country that would not be ruled.
scenes.headline: Would Not Be Ruled

scenes.narration: Fact three. Thailand is the one country in Southeast Asia that was never ruled by a European power.
scenes.headline: Never Colonised

scenes.narration: Britain took land on one side, including Myanmar and Malaysia, and France took Laos and Cambodia on the other.
scenes.headline: Squeezed Between Empires

scenes.narration: Thailand, then called Siam, sat in the middle like a gap on the map.
scenes.headline: A Gap On The Map

scenes.narration: Its kings traded some land, stayed friendly with both sides, and kept the country independent.
scenes.headline: Friends With Both

scenes.narration: The word Thai means free, so Thailand itself means land of the free.
scenes.headline: Land Of The Free

scenes.narration: More than a hundred years ago, the flag of Siam had a white elephant in the middle.
scenes.headline: The Elephant Flag

scenes.narration: Siam is also where the term Siamese twins comes from, because Chang and Eng were born there.
scenes.headline: Siamese Twins

scenes.narration: One kingdom gave the world a cat breed, a twin name, and a flag with an elephant.
scenes.headline: Siam's Gifts

scenes.narration: But history is not the strange part anymore. Next, a market where a train drives through your shop.
scenes.headline: Train Through A Shop

scenes.narration: Yes, through the shop, and the shopkeepers have only moments to move.
scenes.headline: Moments To Move

scenes.narration: Fact four. At Maeklong, a real train runs straight through a fruit and vegetable market, several times a day.
scenes.headline: Train In The Market

scenes.narration: Vendors set up their stalls right on the railway tracks, with baskets of food inches from the rails.
scenes.headline: Stalls On The Tracks

scenes.narration: When the horn sounds, they fold back their awnings and pull their goods away in moments.
scenes.headline: Awnings Fold Back

scenes.narration: The train rolls through slowly, close enough to touch the crates on either side.
scenes.headline: Close Enough To Touch

scenes.narration: Then it passes, the awnings go back up, and customers walk across the tracks as if nothing happened.
scenes.headline: Business As Usual

scenes.narration: If you like strange places like this, subscribe, because we have a lot more of them coming.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places

scenes.narration: Tourists stand on the tracks to film it, and locals just carry on selling chillies and fish.
scenes.headline: Locals Keep Selling

scenes.narration: It is a working railway and a working market, and both have simply learned to share.
scenes.headline: Sharing The Track

scenes.narration: Next up, Thailand's capital, and a name that does not fit on a signboard.
scenes.headline: A Name Too Long

scenes.narration: Locals do not even use it, and that is the clue.
scenes.headline: Nobody Says It

scenes.narration: Fact five. Bangkok is not what Thai people call their capital, and its real name is enormous.
scenes.headline: Not Called Bangkok

scenes.narration: Thais say Krung Thep, which means city of angels, and that is the short version.
scenes.headline: City Of Angels

scenes.narration: The full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world, full of Sanskrit and Pali words.
scenes.headline: A Giant Name

scenes.narration: Thai children even learn a song that helps them recite it.
scenes.headline: A Song To Learn It

scenes.narration: Foreigners kept saying Bangkok, so that name stuck on every map and airline ticket outside Thailand.
scenes.headline: Why Bangkok Stuck

scenes.narration: Big cities usually hide their wildlife, but Bangkok does not, because large monitor lizards walk around its parks.
scenes.headline: Lizards In The City

scenes.narration: In Lumphini Park, they sunbathe on the paths and swim in the ponds, right beside joggers.
scenes.headline: Lizards Beside Joggers

scenes.narration: Office workers eat lunch on the grass while the lizards stroll past like they own the place.
scenes.headline: Lunch With Lizards

scenes.narration: And if lizards are not strange enough, the next place hands out a feast to monkeys.
scenes.headline: A Feast For Monkeys

scenes.narration: A whole town does it on purpose, once a year.
scenes.headline: On Purpose

scenes.narration: Fact six. In Lopburi, people lay out a banquet every November for the town's wild monkeys.
scenes.headline: The Monkey Banquet

scenes.narration: Tables of fruit, sweets and vegetables are stacked into towers, and the monkeys climb straight in.
scenes.headline: Towers Of Fruit

scenes.narration: It is called the Monkey Buffet Festival, and locals hold it to say thank you to the monkeys.
scenes.headline: Monkey Buffet Festival

scenes.narration: The monkeys live around old temple ruins in the middle of town, which are among the city's top sights.
scenes.headline: Monkeys In Temples

scenes.narration: They snatch snacks and sit on parked scooters, and shops often put up nets and cages to protect their goods.
scenes.headline: Monkeys On Scooters

scenes.narration: Visitors are told to keep bags closed, because a monkey will open anything it can reach.
scenes.headline: Keep Bags Closed

scenes.narration: In this town, the animals are the residents, and humans are the guests.
scenes.headline: Guests In Their Town

scenes.narration: So far you have seen a calendar from the future, a borrowed epic, a train in a market, and monkeys at a buffet.
scenes.headline: So Far

scenes.narration: But the strangest one is a road rule. Thailand drives on the left, exactly like India, so you would feel at home at the wheel.
scenes.headline: Left Side, Like India

scenes.narration: That is why the last fact will confuse your brain, even if you drive every day.
scenes.headline: Your Brain Will Glitch

scenes.narration: Fact seven. The Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, where cars change sides of the road on the bridge itself.
scenes.headline: The Friendship Bridge

scenes.narration: It crosses the Mekong river between Nong Khai in Thailand and Vientiane, the capital of Laos.
scenes.headline: Nong Khai To Vientiane

scenes.narration: Thailand drives on the left, the same as India, but Laos drives on the right.
scenes.headline: Left Meets Right

scenes.narration: So somewhere on this one structure, traffic has to swap sides without anyone crashing.
scenes.headline: Swap Without Crashing

scenes.narration: Road signs and markings guide each car from one side to the other, over the water.
scenes.headline: Signs Guide The Switch

scenes.narration: Drivers start the bridge on the left and finish it on the right, with a river under them.
scenes.headline: Start Left, End Right

scenes.narration: The Mekong below is one of Asia's great rivers, running along or through Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam.
scenes.headline: The Mighty Mekong

scenes.narration: Your hands know the left side, so for a moment your brain has to learn the road again.
scenes.headline: Relearn The Road

scenes.narration: Most borders change a flag or a language, but this one changes which side of the road keeps you safe.
scenes.headline: More Than A Flag

scenes.narration: That is seven facts: a year of 2569, a city named for Ayodhya, a country nobody ruled, and a train in a market.
scenes.headline: Seven True Facts

scenes.narration: Then a city of angels with lizards in its parks, monkeys at a buffet, and a bridge that flips the road.
scenes.headline: All Of It Is Real

scenes.narration: So remember: your car really does swap sides of the road on a bridge between Thailand and Laos.
scenes.headline: Back To The Bridge

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: another country that looks normal on a map and is not.
scenes.headline: Next: Another Country
